Profile every column of a set of tables

Source: R/profile.R
db_profile.Rd

Artefact 2 of the roadmap. For each column: null rate, distinct count, min and max, mean (numeric), string lengths, top values, uniqueness, an inferred semantic type and two fingerprint hashes. Large tables are profiled on a sample. Results can be checkpointed per table into a store so that an interrupted run resumes where it stopped.

Usage

db_profile(
  con,
  inventory = NULL,
  tables = NULL,
  sample_rows = 1e+06,
  top_n = 10,
  full_set_max = 50,
  top_values_max_distinct = 10000,
  keep_values = FALSE,
  store = NULL,
  resume = TRUE,
  column_batch = 40,
  dialect = NULL,
  progress = interactive()
)

Arguments

con

A DBIConnection.

inventory

A db_inventory from db_inventory(). If NULL one is built first (row counts are needed to decide on sampling).

tables

Optional subset of inventory$tables to profile.

sample_rows

Tables with more rows than this are profiled on a sample of roughly this many rows. Inf disables sampling, which is the faster choice on DuckDB and Parquet, where aggregates over the full table cost less than materialising a sample; the threshold is for engines such as SQL Server where a full scan is the expensive part.

top_n

How many most-frequent values to record per column.

full_set_max

Columns with at most this many distinct values have every value recorded, not just the top top_n, so that a code list's frequency table is complete and foreign key membership can be tested against it.

top_values_max_distinct

Only compute top values for columns with at most this many distinct values; beyond that a frequency table says little.

keep_values

If FALSE (the default) the literal min, max and top values of columns inferred as identifiers or free text, or whose names suggest personal data, are suppressed and only their hashes kept. Set TRUE on a system where the profile output is itself safe to hold.

store

Optional path to a SQLite store (see store_open()). Each table's profile is written as soon as it finishes.

resume

If TRUE and store is given, tables already profiled successfully in the store are skipped.

column_batch

Number of columns aggregated in one query. Lower it if the engine rejects very wide statements.

dialect

Optional dialect override, see db_dialect().

progress

Show a progress bar? Default TRUE in interactive use.

Value

A tibble of class column_profile, one row per column. Columns include null_rate, distinct_count, distinct_rate, is_unique, pk_candidate (unique, never null and a string, integer or uuid type; on a sampled table this is evidence from the sample only), fk_candidate, fk_target, fk_confidence and fk_evidence (see infer_foreign_keys(); inferred across the tables profiled in this call, or across the whole store by inventory_run()), min_value, max_value, mean_value, min_length, max_length, mean_length, true_count, top_values (JSON), top_values_hash, semantic_type, values_suppressed, value_fingerprint, column_fingerprint, rows_profiled, sampled, sample_method, profiled_at.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- fakehospdata::fh_connect("sample")
inv <- db_inventory(con, include = "pas_patients", progress = FALSE)
prof <- db_profile(con, inv, progress = FALSE)
prof[, c("column_name", "null_rate", "distinct_count", "semantic_type")]
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
} # }
